digest.en: Foreign Secretary Misri’s first high‑level trip since the new Nepali government took office dominates this hour, with talks in Kathmandu slated for next week.
digest.hi: ईरान ने पड़ोसी देशों पर हमले का दावा खारिज किया, जबकि अमेरिका ने इसे झूठा बता दिया। इसी बीच चीन ने फैक्ट्रियों में एआई के उपयोग पर 18 सूत्रीय नियंत्रण लागू कर दिया।

articles.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on
articles.summary: India's Foreign Secretary Misri visits Nepal to discuss Prime Minister Balendra Shah's upcoming trip. The talks cover appointing a new Nepali ambassador to India. Officials also plan disaster assistance measures following recent flash floods in the region. Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda.

articles.title: Arrests, Resignations, Repainting: Here's What's Happening In Postelection Serbia
articles.summary: Serbia's political landscape shifted rapidly after Student List won the October 25 parliamentary elections. Former President Aleksandar Vucic was ousted from power after more than a decade. The week brought arrests, resignations, and significant administrative changes across the government. Events have moved fast since Student List won Serbia’s parliamentary elections on October 25. Here are some of the notable happenings that have unfolded in the week since former President Aleksandar Vucic was ousted from office after more than a decade in power.

articles.title: After A Crushing Defeat, What Now For Serbia's Vucic?
articles.summary: Aleksandar Vucic stated he will return to power after his October election defeat. Legal challenges now threaten his political future. Prosecutors may pursue criminal charges against the former leader. His path back to office faces significant judicial hurdles. Former longstanding Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic has said he’ll “come back” after losing elections in October. But is his future more likely to be in a court dock instead of the court of public opinion?

articles.title: Israel’s intent is to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group: Justice Muralidhar
articles.summary: Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry, accused Israel of preventing Palestinian existence. He stated Israel seeks to expand occupation while reducing the population. The findings condemn policies in occupied Palestinian territories. In a strong indictment of Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry, has accused Israel of seeking to expand its occupation while reducing the Palestinian population.

articles.title: Is Europe In Iran's Crosshairs? Tehran Hints At Wider Military Reach
articles.summary: Iran's supreme leader stated any future response to an attack would have no geographical limits. The remarks suggest Tehran may abandon its 2,000-kilometer missile range limit. Analysts speculate Europe could now fall within Iran's military reach. A statement attributed to Iran's supreme leader says any future response to an attack would have no geographical limits. The remarks have fueled speculation that Tehran could target Europe and abandon its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on missile range.

articles.title: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
articles.summary: UNESCO reports that six in seven journalist murders go unpunished. Global impunity for these killings has risen for the first time in over a decade. The organization also flags the growing use of drones as an emerging threat to reporters working in active conflict zones. Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.

articles.title: What are U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: The United States holds midterm elections on November 3 to determine control of Congress. Voters decide all 435 House seats, one-third of the Senate, and many governorships. The outcome directly weakens or strengthens the President’s legislative agenda based on which party prevails. The U. S. midterm elections on November 3 determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats, about one-third of the 100 Senate seats, and numerous state governorships up for grabs, in a nationwide vote that weakens or strengthens the President’s agenda depending on which party prevails.

articles.title: Energy is America’s real weapon in a multipolar world
articles.summary: The United States is shifting its strategic focus from broad technological dominance to control over oil and gas. Washington now treats global energy supplies as its primary instrument of influence. Disrupting or threatening these finite commodities has become a central tool in a multipolar world. Faced with an emerging multipolar order, the United States appears to be relying less on dominance of every frontier technology than on leveraging its influence over the world’s most finite and strategically vital commodities: oil and gas.

articles.title: Trump’s Republicans brace for a midterm shellacking
articles.summary: US Republicans face a potentially punishing verdict in Tuesday's midterm elections. President Trump's approval rating stands at 32 percent in a recent poll. Democrats lead the national congressional ballot by more than eight percentage points, shifting the electoral map against the administration. WASHINGTON, D. C. US President Donald Trump’s Republicans enter Tuesday’s midterm elections facing a potentially punishing voter verdict. His approval rating stands at just 32% in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll, while Democrats lead the national congressional ballot by more than eight percentage points.

articles.title: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends
articles.summary: António Guterres stated the UN remains committed to a political solution in Western Sahara. The organization supports the self-determination of the local population. This statement coincided with the wind-down of the MINURSO peacekeeping mission. The UN signaled continued diplomatic backing for the region. The UN remains committed to supporting a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara that provides for the self-determination of its people, Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, as the UN peacekeeping mission there began to wind down.

articles.title: Binance resumes customer withdrawals after record $6.3bn hack
articles.summary: Binance resumed customer withdrawals after a record $6.3 billion hack. The exchange stated that 90 percent of the losses are covered. The FBI attributed the theft to a North Korean state-sponsored group. This marks the largest cryptocurrency heist in history. Cryptocurrency exchange says 90% of losses covered as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitorThe cryptocurrency exchange Binance has started to allow its customers to withdraw their funds from the platform, as it recovers from a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack. The exchange was hit by the theft on Thursday, which has since been described as the biggest heist in history, with experts.

articles.title: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Cooperation In Challenge To US
articles.summary: Chinese and Russian leaders met in St. Petersburg to deepen Arctic cooperation. The summit focused on challenging United States influence in the region. Beijing and Moscow are coordinating to expand their strategic presence. This move directly confronts Western allies in the Arctic. The 31st meeting of the Chinese and Russian heads of government held in St. Petersburg on October 21 was notable for its focus on cooperation in the Arctic, where Beijing and Moscow are increasingly challenging the United States and its allies.

articles.title: Rubio Casts Doubts On Quick Deal To End War In Ukraine, Defends Russian Contacts
articles.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he was unsure a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine is possible and that Russian President Vladimir Putin may skip the December G20 summit in Miami, according to European US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he was unsure whether a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine was possible, while European officials told RFE/RL the top US diplomat privately expressed doubts that Russian President Vladimir Putin will attend December’s Miami G20 summit.

articles.title: Tears Of Joy As Ukrainians Evacuated From Russian-Occupied Oleshky Reunite With Family
articles.summary: Hundreds of residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunited with family in Ukrainian territory. A convoy of 25 buses facilitated the transfer after a US-brokered cease-fire. The residents had lived under occupation for nearly four years. After nearly four years under Russian occupation, hundreds of residents from the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky have arrived in Ukrainian-controlled territory following a cease-fire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump.

articles.title: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi
articles.summary: UN human rights chief Michelle Bachelet demanded an independent probe into the death of a Yemeni UN staffer held by the Houthis for over two years. The family learned of his death only weeks after it occurred. Bachelet stated the family deserved to know the truth. The incident highlights ongoing detention practices by the Yemeni armed group. The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague held by the Houthis for more than two years, whose family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.

articles.title: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
articles.summary: A UN rights official stated North Korea is more isolated than ever despite internal development. The country is building infrastructure and rolling out mobile banking. However, its population remains cut off from the outside world. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate.

articles.title: Kosovo Protests Grow Over Killing Of Woman Who Pleaded For Police Protection
articles.summary: A woman in Kosovo was killed by her brother‑in‑law after she repeatedly asked police for protection. The prosecutor declined to act on a death threat, sparking protests across the country. Protests are spreading across Kosovo after a woman who repeatedly pleaded for protection was killed, allegedly by her brother-in-law. An official investigation found multiple institutional failures, including a prosecutor's refusal to act on a death threat.

articles.title: How crypto hacking funds isolated North Korea’s nuclear programme
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency theft generates roughly half of North Korea's foreign currency income. The isolated state relies on sophisticated hacking to fund its nuclear program. Experts attribute significant digital thefts to state-sponsored actors. Cryptocurrency theft is estimated to generate half of the country’s foreign currency incomeNorth Korea plays by its own rules. articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro’s short-lived ‘president-elect’ claim met with mockery
articles.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro fled to the United States after losing the Brazilian election. He declared himself president-elect for 58 minutes. Media ridiculed the move as shameful. His letter contained the wrong coat of arms. The stunt ended in mockery. Brazilian media ridicule defeated candidate over ‘shameful’ absconsion to US and bizarre letter with wrong coat of armsFlávio Bolsonaro had hoped that by Sunday night people would be calling him the next president of Brazil. Instead, the far-right politician’s decision to flee to the US after losing the election and – for 58 minutes – to declare himself “Brazil’s true president-elect”, has made him.

articles.title: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
articles.summary: The UN human rights office warned of a deepening displacement crisis in Gaza. Israeli forces are pushing Palestinians into smaller areas while destroying infrastructure. Attacks on displacement sites continue. The office expressed concern over actions resembling ethnic cleansing. Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.

articles.title: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
articles.summary: Over twenty-eight million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo face food insecurity. The IPC warns this number will rise in coming months. Conflict, Ebola outbreaks, and climate shocks are driving the deepening hunger crisis. More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.

articles.title: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
articles.summary: UNHCR reported that over 280,000 people have been displaced by fighting in Yemen. Many vulnerable residents cannot access lifesaving relief because the conflict makes travel too dangerous. The agency highlighted the growing gap between need and delivery in the ongoing crisis. More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

articles.title: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
articles.summary: The UN humanitarian chief stated the Oleshky ceasefire offers hope for civilians. He emphasized that residents must be able to leave safely and voluntarily. Attacks on aid vehicles continue despite the pause in fighting. Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

articles.title: Severe rainfall and flood warnings issued for central Greece and western Turkey
articles.summary: Powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado struck Turkey this week. Heavy rain and strong winds will continue affecting south-eastern Europe and Turkey for several days. A low-pressure system is driving the severe weather across the region. Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expectedHeavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms.

articles.title: Will Trump Help Putin Win in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Crisis Group experts discussed the growing rift between Washington and Kyiv. The conversation covered Russia's intensifying attacks on Ukrainian territory. European capitals are working to strengthen Ukraine's defenses. These efforts occur while Europe faces its own internal pressures. This week on Hold Your Fire!, Richard speaks with Crisis Group experts Lucian Kim, Stephen Pomper and Fabienne Hara about the latest rift between Washington and Kyiv, Russia’s intensifying attacks and European capitals’ efforts to strengthen Ukraine while themselves under pressure.

articles.title: 'ईरान पर न्यूक्लियर अटैक करेंगे ट्रंप', टकर कार्लसन की चेतावनी से मची खलबली, कौन सा बम गिरा सकता है
articles.summary: टकर कार्लसन ने दावा किया कि नेतन्याहू ट्रंप पर ईरान के अंडरग्राउंड ठिकानों पर हमले का दबाव बना रहे हैं। इस बहस में B61-11 परमाणु बम और मदर ऑफ ऑल बॉम्ब्स के नाम सामने आए हैं। Nuclear Attack On Iran: ईरान के पिकैक्स माउंटेन स्थित गहरे अंडरग्राउंड ठिकाने को लेकर अमेरिका के संभावित हमले की चर्चा तेज है. टकर कार्लसन ने दावा किया है कि इजरायल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू, डोनाल्ड ट्रंप पर सैन्य कार्रवाई का दबाव बना रहे हैं.

articles.summary: ईरान ने होर्मुज स्ट्रेट पर अमेरिकी नौसैनिक उपस्थिति को समझौते की शर्त बना दिया है। ट्रंप ने जलमार्ग को अपना नियंत्रण मानते हुए नाम बदलने का दावा किया है। दोनों देशों के बीच तनाव बढ़ गया है। इस रणनीतिक जलमार्ग पर हमेशा से ही ईरान का कंट्रोल रहा है, लेकिन अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप (Donald Trump) पिछले कुछ समय से इसे ‘ट्रंप स्ट्रेट’ (Strait of Trump) बता रहे हैं और दावा कर रहे हैं कि इस पर अमेरिकी नेवी का कंट्रोल है।

articles.title: कच्चे अंडे की तरह टूट जाएंगे अमेरिकी एयरक्राफ्ट कैरियर, चीन ने बनाई 'कैरियर किलर' DF-26B मिसाइल
articles.summary: चीन की DF-26B मिसाइल का वीडियो वायरल हुआ है। इसे अमेरिकी विमानवाहक पोतों के लिए खतरा माना जाता है। मिसाइल की लंबी दूरी और मोबाइल लॉन्चर इसकी ताकत हैं। चलते पोत को निशाना बनाना कठिन है। चीन की DF-26B 'कैरियर किलर' मिसाइल का वीडियो 1 नवंबर 2026 को फिर वायरल हुआ. हालांकि, यह फुटेज दिसंबर 2024 में भी प्रसारित हो चुका है.

articles.summary: 1917 में ब्रिटिश सरकार ने बालफोर डिक्लेरेशन जारी किया। इस दस्तावेज में केवल 67 शब्द थे। यह पत्र इजरायल की नींव रखने वाला माना जाता है और इसने मध्य पूर्व की राजनीति को स्थायी रूप से बदल दिया। 2 नवंबर यानी आज के ही दिन 1917 को इजरायल की नींव कागजों पर पड़ी थी. किसे पता था कि यह दस्तावेज मिडिल ईस्ट की नींव बदलने वाला साबित होगा.

articles.title: लाल सागर के पास तेल के पोर्ट पर सऊदी अरब ने किया हवाई हमला, यमन में भी की एयरस्ट्राइक
articles.summary: सऊदी अरब ने यमन के हूती विद्रोहियों के ठिकानों पर हवाई हमले किए। लाल सागर के पास तेल के पोर्ट पर भी एयरस्ट्राइक की गई। हूतियों और सऊदी सेना के बीच क्षेत्रीय तनाव बढ़ रहा है। यमन (Yemen) के हूती विद्रोहियों (Houthis) और देश की सरकारी सेना के बीच जंग जारी है। दोनों पक्ष लगातार एक-दूसरे के कब्ज़े वाले इलाकों पर हमले कर रहे हैं और एक-दूसरे को नुकसान पहुंचा रहे हैं।

articles.title: पाकिस्तान-अफगानिस्तान सीमा पर फिर टकराव, तालिबान का सवाल- बातचीत से भाग क्यों रहा इस्लामाबाद?
articles.summary: पाकिस्तान-अफगानिस्तान सीमा पर दक्षिण वजीरिस्तान में तालिबान चौकियों से फायरिंग का दावा किया गया। पाकिस्तानी सुरक्षा बलों ने जवाब में कई ठिकानों को निशाना बनाया। अफगान यूनाइटेड फ्रंट ने आठ प्रांतों में 16 हमलों का दावा किया है। पाकिस्तान और अफगानिस्तान के बीच सीमा पर तनाव एक बार फिर बढ़ गया है. दक्षिण वजीरिस्तान के अंगूर अड्डा इलाके में अफगान तालिबान की चौकियों से फायरिंग का दावा किया गया है.
